bundles.title: Pre-procedure check (anaesthesia)
bundles.description: Anaesthetic assessment before surgery, sedation or a procedure under anaesthesia.
bundles.note: Task before role: the same bundle serves anaesthetist, pre-assessment nurse and, with modifiers, surgeon.

why_overrides.med_antithrombotic: Bleeding risk and choice of anaesthetic technique. Show drug, dose, schedule and as-of date.
why_overrides.allergies: Drug, latex and contrast reactions before anything is given.
why_overrides.lvef: Cardiac reserve before anaesthesia. Show value, date and the echo wording.
why_overrides.hba1c: NICE NG45 asks whether HbA1c was tested in the last 3 months, so the date matters as much as the value.
why_overrides.kidney_function: Drug dosing; NICE NG45 links kidney testing to comorbidity. Often not documented.

bundles.title: Surgical planning after tumour board

bundles.note: Receptors and Ki-67 are P1 here and absent from B01: this contrast is the demo of 'the screen changes with the role'.

why_overrides.tumour_site_laterality: Side is the most expensive thing to get wrong; also feeds contradiction checks.

roles.name: Anaesthetist
roles.typical_situations: Pre-operative visit; sedation for a procedure; regional or neuraxial planning; post-operative review.
roles.mindset: Is it safe to anaesthetise, and what has to be managed around the procedure: bleeding, allergy, cardiac reserve, airway, glucose.
roles.often_missing: Kidney function, airway assessment, earlier anaesthesia problems, time of last blood-thinner dose.

roles.name: Surgeon (breast / general)
roles.typical_situations: Planning after tumour board; consent; post-operative complication review.
roles.mindset: Exactly what is operated on, which side, what stage and biology, and what could complicate surgery.
roles.often_missing: Axillary status, staging imaging, earlier cancer treatment.

roles.name: Radiation oncologist
roles.typical_situations: IORT or external-beam planning; boost decisions.
roles.mindset: Where and how much to treat: side, site, stage, earlier radiotherapy, implanted devices.

roles.name: Medical oncologist
roles.typical_situations: Adjuvant therapy discussion; tumour board preparation.
roles.mindset: Tumour biology and fitness for systemic therapy: receptors, stage, heart, kidney, liver, blood counts.
roles.often_missing: Kidney, liver and blood counts; performance status.

roles.name: Vascular surgeon
roles.typical_situations: Carotid disease review; carotid endarterectomy consideration.
roles.mindset: Degree, side and symptoms of the stenosis, imaging, and antiplatelet cover.

roles.name: Pre-assessment nurse
roles.typical_situations: Nurse-led pre-operative screening.
roles.mindset: What the anaesthetic team will ask: allergies, drugs, function, home support.

roles.name: Emergency physician
roles.typical_situations: Neurological or visual symptoms; chest pain; allergic reaction; hypo- or hyperglycaemia.
roles.mindset: What could explain the presentation, what is dangerous to give, and what the patient already takes.
roles.often_missing: Kidney function, current glucose, time of last antithrombotic dose.

roles.name: Paramedic / triage nurse
roles.typical_situations: Pre-hospital handover; triage.
roles.mindset: Fast safety handover: allergies, blood thinners, main diagnoses, medication, resuscitation wishes.

roles.name: Neurologist / stroke unit
roles.typical_situations: TIA or stroke work-up; carotid symptom attribution.
roles.mindset: Prior events, vascular findings, antithrombotics, rhythm, risk factors and baseline deficits.
roles.often_missing: ECG or rhythm monitoring, neurological baseline, head imaging report.

roles.name: Radiologist / radiographer
roles.typical_situations: Contrast CT or angiography request check.
roles.mindset: Contrast safety: reactions, kidney function, metformin, earlier imaging.

roles.name: General practitioner
roles.typical_situations: Diabetes review; hypertension review; open follow-ups; medication review; weight loss.
roles.mindset: Longitudinal control and loose ends: values over time, doses, and what was supposed to happen next. The task picks the bundle.
roles.often_missing: Later values after discharge; kidney function; completion of follow-ups.

roles.name: Diabetologist / endocrinologist
roles.typical_situations: Diabetes review; peri-operative diabetes plan.
roles.mindset: Glycaemic control, drug regimen, hypoglycaemia and complications.

roles.name: Cardiologist
roles.typical_situations: Blood pressure and heart-function review; pre-operative cardiac question.
roles.mindset: Pump function, rhythm, blood pressure control, ischaemic disease, vascular risk.

roles.name: Pharmacist
roles.typical_situations: Medication reconciliation; prescribing safety review.
roles.mindset: Accurate, complete list; doses; changes; allergies; kidney function; interactions.
roles.often_missing: Kidney and liver function, stop dates.

roles.name: Ophthalmologist
roles.typical_situations: Transient vision loss; diabetic or hypertensive eye review.
roles.mindset: Visual events, their side, vascular and diabetic causes, and eye follow-up.

roles.name: Dentist
roles.typical_situations: Extraction or minor oral surgery.
roles.mindset: Bleeding risk, allergies, valve disease, diabetes control.

roles.name: Ward nurse
roles.typical_situations: Admission assessment; discharge handover.
roles.mindset: Safe admission and discharge: allergies, medication, mobility, follow-ups, support.

roles.name: Physiotherapist
roles.typical_situations: Post-operative rehab after breast surgery.
roles.mindset: Side and type of surgery, function, cardiac limits, bleeding risk.

roles.name: Dietitian
roles.typical_situations: Weight loss; diabetes diet advice.
roles.mindset: Weight trajectory, diagnoses, glucose-lowering drugs and appetite.

roles.name: Admitting physician (medical)
roles.typical_situations: Medical admission; unfamiliar presentation.
roles.mindset: Complete picture of diagnoses, drugs, allergies and recent stays.
roles.often_missing: Anything not in the letters; a visible note says so.

For each recommendation search for evidence it happened; none found is 'not documented'.

Show the label panel for the ingredient (section 11): listed contraindications beside the related patient facts (found, documented as none, or not documented). Never state that a drug is contraindicated for this patient.

consistency_checks.name: BMI recomputation
consistency_checks.method: BMI = kg / m^2 using height and weight from the same letter.
consistency_checks.false_alarm_guard: Tolerance 0.5 kg/m^2 for rounding. Different letters are not compared.

consistency_checks.name: Age against date of birth
consistency_checks.method: Compute age at the document date (and at the anchor date) from the date of birth; compare with any stated age. Never use the age field in patient.json (it is today's age).
consistency_checks.false_alarm_guard: Only flag if the gap is 1 year or more.

consistency_checks.name: Laterality conflict
consistency_checks.method: Extract side tokens (links, rechts, beidseits, left, right) per finding; compare for the same finding.
consistency_checks.false_alarm_guard: Same finding and same time frame only; 'both' vs one side is shown as a note, not an alarm.

consistency_checks.name: Event date conflict
consistency_checks.method: Same event type and entity with two different dates.
consistency_checks.false_alarm_guard: Month-year is compatible with a full date in that month; planned vs actual are different events.

consistency_checks.name: Dose conflict
consistency_checks.method: Same drug with different dose in documents from the same time window.
consistency_checks.false_alarm_guard: Dose changes across time are not contradictions; compare only within 7 days or the same letter.

consistency_checks.name: Allergy status conflict
consistency_checks.method: 'keine bekannten Allergien' next to a listed allergen in the same time window.
consistency_checks.false_alarm_guard: Allergy later documented is a change over time, not a conflict.

consistency_checks.name: HbA1c unit consistency
consistency_checks.method: IFCC mmol/mol = (NGSP % - 2.15) x 10.929; compare when both units appear for one test.
consistency_checks.false_alarm_guard: Flag only if the converted values differ by 2 mmol/mol or more.

consistency_checks.name: T category against tumour size
consistency_checks.method: Breast: T1 up to 20 mm, T2 over 20 up to 50 mm, T3 over 50 mm.
consistency_checks.false_alarm_guard: Same pathology report only; clinical vs pathological size differences are false alarms.

consistency_checks.name: EF value against wording
consistency_checks.method: Numeric EF against words such as normal or reduced.
consistency_checks.false_alarm_guard: Gross mismatches only; thresholds vary between sources.

consistency_checks.name: Negated vs affirmed diagnosis
consistency_checks.method: 'kein / ohne X' beside 'X' for the same time window.
consistency_checks.false_alarm_guard: Resolved or historical diagnoses ('Z.n.') are changes over time.

guidelines.title: Routine preoperative tests for elective surgery (NG45)
guidelines.era_vs_april_2016: Contemporary: published the same month as the case (text since updated)
guidelines.supports: Ties tests to comorbidity. HbA1c section 1.6 (offer to people with diabetes not tested in the last 3 months); echocardiography section 1.9; also kidney function, haemostasis and ECG.
guidelines.note: Excludes cardiothoracic surgery, neurosurgery and pregnancy. Check the surgery-grade and ASA tables.

guidelines.title: Präoperative Evaluation erwachsener Patienten vor elektiven, nicht herz-thoraxchirurgischen Eingriffen. Gemeinsame Empfehlung DGAI, DGCH, DGIM
guidelines.era_vs_april_2016: 2017 edition is closest to 2016; 2024 is current
guidelines.supports: Part A general principles, Part B extended diagnostics, Part C handling of long-term medication (feeds the antithrombotic, antidiabetic and ARB rules).
guidelines.note: German societies: check whether an Austrian society endorses it before calling it Austrian.

guidelines.title: Präoperative Blutungsanamnese (Pfanner et al.)
guidelines.era_vs_april_2016: Older than the case; check for an update
guidelines.supports: Recommends a standardised bleeding-history questionnaire; patients on coagulation-relevant drugs need laboratory tests, starting with platelet count (supports bleeding-history, coagulation and blood-count slots).
guidelines.note: The excerpt seen was cut off after the platelet count; read the paper for the full parameter list.

guidelines.title: ÖGARI working-group guideline on pre-operative evaluation (two-category risk scheme: minor vs major surgery)
guidelines.supports: Described in a Swiss guideline (IHAMZ) as an Austrian working-group guideline; the primary ÖGARI document was not located.
guidelines.note: Do not show on screen until the primary source is found. The link below is the Swiss secondary source.

guidelines.title: Diabetes mellitus - Leitlinien für die Praxis (ÖDG)
guidelines.version: Wien Klin Wochenschr; editions seen: 2007, 2009, 2012, 2019, 2023 (vol 135, Suppl 1); 2026 pocket guide
guidelines.era_vs_april_2016: Edition in force in April 2016 not yet identified (the 2012 foreword announced the next edition for 2015)
guidelines.supports: Diabetes review: drugs, targets, complications. The 2026 pocket guide states it summarises the sixth full revision.
guidelines.note: Locate the 2015/2016 edition for a period-correct citation; the 2023 text is current.

guidelines.title: Pre-operative evaluation of adults undergoing elective noncardiac surgery: updated guideline from the ESA (De Hert et al.); 2025 ESAIC update
guidelines.version: Eur J Anaesthesiol 2018;35(6):407-465 (literature search to May 2016); update 2025;42(1):1-35
guidelines.supports: General pre-operative assessment framework. The 2025 update gives 55 recommendations agreed by Delphi vote.
guidelines.note: Choose one edition and label it with its year. 2025 update DOI: 10.1097/EJA.0000000000002069.

guidelines.title: ESC/ESA guidelines on non-cardiac surgery: cardiovascular assessment and management (2014); ESC guidelines on non-cardiac surgery (2022)
guidelines.supports: 2014 text highlights functional capacity and is the first to recommend peri-operative regimens for dual antiplatelet therapy and new oral anticoagulants. 2022 key messages stress patient-reported functional capacity and antithrombotic management.
guidelines.note: Use 2014 for period-correct citations and 2022 for current practice.

guidelines.title: Stroke and transient ischaemic attack in over 16s: diagnosis and initial management (NG128)
guidelines.era_vs_april_2016: Later than the case; recommendations tagged [2008] were in force in 2016
guidelines.supports: Rec 1.1.2: exclude hypoglycaemia as the cause of sudden-onset neurological symptoms [2008]. Rec 1.1.4: aspirin 300 mg for suspected TIA [2019]. Includes imaging for suspected TIA.
guidelines.note: Cite recommendation numbers with their [year] tags.

guidelines.title: Hypertension in adults: diagnosis and management (NG136)
guidelines.version: Published 28 Aug 2019; last updated 21 Nov 2023 (replaced CG127, 24 Aug 2011)
guidelines.era_vs_april_2016: Later than the case; CG127 was in force in 2016
guidelines.supports: Blood pressure measurement, diagnosis and treatment; also replaces the blood pressure section of NG28.
guidelines.note: A 2024 ESC hypertension guideline also exists; choose one and label it.

guidelines.title: Type 2 diabetes in adults: management (NG28)
guidelines.version: Published 2 Dec 2015; last updated Feb 2026 (replaced CG87)
guidelines.era_vs_april_2016: Contemporary in its 2015 form; the text has since been revised
guidelines.supports: Section 1.6 blood glucose management including individual HbA1c targets; rec 1.5.1: do not offer aspirin or clopidogrel to adults with type 2 diabetes without cardiovascular disease [2015].
guidelines.note: Check which recommendations changed after 2015 before citing a section.

guidelines.title: Early and locally advanced breast cancer: diagnosis and management (NG101)
guidelines.era_vs_april_2016: Later than the case; carries 2009 recommendations that were in force in 2016
guidelines.supports: Rec 1.3.1: assess ER, PR and HER2 together at initial histopathological diagnosis [2018]. Rec 1.2.1: pre-treatment ultrasound of the axilla [2009]. Sections on surgery, radiotherapy and systemic therapy planning.
guidelines.note: Cite recommendation numbers with their [year] tags.

guidelines.title: Acute kidney injury: prevention, detection and management (NG148)
guidelines.version: Published 18 Dec 2019; last updated 16 Oct 2024 (replaced CG169, 2013)
guidelines.era_vs_april_2016: Later than the case; CG169 was in force in 2016
guidelines.supports: 2024 contrast recommendations: do not delay iodine-based contrast in a clinically significant emergency; before non-urgent contrast CT assess for existing kidney disease (1.1.8); if screening is negative and the person is stable, proceeding without further blood tests may be considered (1.1.9).
guidelines.note: This softens how hard the contrast bundle should push kidney tests: show kidney function if documented, never imply contrast must wait for it.

guidelines.title: Drug allergy: diagnosis and management (CG183)
guidelines.supports: Names poor documentation of drug allergy as a major issue and aims to ensure allergies are recorded properly (supports the allergy slot and the split between 'documented as none' and 'not documented').
guidelines.note: Recommendation numbers were not read; cite the guideline, not a numbered recommendation, until checked.

guidelines.title: Contrast media safety: ESUR guidelines (contrast nephropathy 2011; post-contrast AKI recommendations 2018, in guideline version 10)
guidelines.supports: 2011: patients with eGFR 60 or above can continue metformin. 2018: stop metformin from the time of contrast if eGFR is below 30. Also covers risk factors, hydration and dialysis.
guidelines.note: Verify exact thresholds in the full text before any on-screen wording; the app shows facts, not threshold advice.

guidelines.title: Medicines optimisation: the safe and effective use of medicines to enable the best possible outcomes (NG5)
guidelines.supports: Covers medicines reconciliation, medication review and decision aids for people taking one or more medicines.
guidelines.note: UK guideline: label it as such.

guidelines.title: Perioperative care in adults (NG180)
guidelines.supports: Covers all phases of perioperative care for adults having elective or emergency surgery, including dental surgery.
guidelines.note: Supplementary for bundles B01 and B15.

guidelines.title: Austrian society guidelines still to locate: stroke/TIA, general hypertension, breast cancer treatment
guidelines.supports: Nothing confirmed yet.
guidelines.note: Search the Austrian stroke, hypertension and senology societies. Do not cite until a document is found.

guidelines.title: No clinical guideline: workflow or documentation purpose; cite local discharge or handover policy
guidelines.supports: Bundles about information completeness rather than a clinical decision.
guidelines.note: State this honestly on screen: 'workflow rationale, no guideline'.

guidelines.title: Individualisierung der antihypertensiven Therapie bei Patienten mit Diabetes mellitus (ÖDG guideline)
guidelines.supports: Austrian guideline on blood pressure treatment in diabetes (ACE inhibitors, or alternatively ARBs, and combination therapy). Supports the blood pressure bundle for patients with diabetes.
guidelines.note: Read the 2023 update before citing any target values.

guidelines.title: Empfehlungen der Österreichischen Gesellschaft für Senologie: Nachsorge nach Mammakarzinom
guidelines.supports: Austrian follow-up recommendations after breast cancer. Supports follow-up slots, not surgical planning.
guidelines.note: Seen in a citation-index record only; open the journal page before citing.

guidelines.title: S3-Leitlinie Früherkennung, Diagnostik, Therapie und Nachsorge des Mammakarzinoms (AWMF register 032-045OL)
guidelines.version: Consultation version 0.4.1 (Aug 2017) seen in citations; later versions exist
guidelines.supports: German-language breast cancer guideline used alongside German and international recommendations; candidate companion to NG101 for surgical-planning slots.
guidelines.note: Existence confirmed from citations only; fetch the current version from AWMF and confirm numbering.

slot_notes.age_sex: Compute age from the date of birth at the anchor date (57 for the demo patient: born 15 March 1959, anchor 15 April 2016). patient.json stores today's age (67): never use it.
slot_notes.weight: Extraction dates are month precision; order values inside a month by document date.
slot_notes.hba1c: The only lab value documented in the record; show month and year.
slot_notes.allergies: cave.json holds one vague entry ('Arzneimittel-Allergie') with no documentIds: use it only as a search trigger and extract the allergen and reaction from the letter text, otherwise the link fails traceability.
slot_notes.kidney_function: Both discharge letters end with an empty lab table and no lab value except HbA1c is documented: show 'not documented' and link the empty table as the searched passage.
slot_notes.electrolytes: Empty lab table in both discharge letters: show 'not documented' with that note.
slot_notes.blood_count: Empty lab table in both discharge letters: show 'not documented' with that note.
slot_notes.coagulation: Empty lab table in both discharge letters: show 'not documented' with that note.
slot_notes.liver_function: Empty lab table in both discharge letters: show 'not documented' with that note.
slot_notes.lipids: Empty lab table in both discharge letters: show 'not documented' with that note.
slot_notes.glucose: Empty lab table in both discharge letters: show 'not documented' with that note.
slot_notes.med_current: Schedules have four numbers (morning, midday, evening, night); show three and decode, for example 1 0 0 0 -> 1-0-0 'once in the morning'. Dose sits inside IBM's matched text; re-read it from the canonical text.
slot_notes.diagnoses_all: IBM statuses: positive, negative (ruled out), suspected, statuspost. Show negative as 'ruled out', suspected as 'suspected', statuspost as 'past'; never list them as confirmed facts.
slot_notes.procedures_all: IBM statuses: positive (done), statuspost, recommended. Only 9 of 62 procedure dates have a day. 'recommended' feeds board and follow-up slots; never show it as done.
slot_notes.discharge_followups: Candidates come from procedures marked 'recommended'; confirm the wording in the letter text.
slot_notes.board_recommendation: Candidates come from procedures marked 'recommended'; confirm the wording in the letter text.
slot_notes.hospital_stays: documents.json stay dates can differ from the letter text; the text wins.
slot_notes.birads: Present in scores-all.json (the data README says 5 means very likely cancer). Compare with histology wording; a mismatch is a contradiction candidate.
slot_notes.carotid_stenosis: Laterality comes from the text only; IBM's matched fragments may be cut or carry markup.

ibm_extraction_ideas.detail: Look up which documents mention a concept, run extraction on those documents only, then validate every quote in the canonical text. Faster and cheaper; the documents stay the source of truth.

documents.json gives type, department and hospital stay. Prefer the pathology report for receptors, the tumour-board letter for the recommendation and discharge letters for follow-ups. Read the file first to confirm the real types.

ibm_extraction_ideas.idea: Use the hospital stay as the unit
ibm_extraction_ideas.detail: 'The June 2015 stay' becomes a deterministic document selection for follow-up questions.
Map each role to ICD-10 areas and ATC groups (table below). A new role then gets a sensible screen without a handwritten bundle, which beats the general-core fallback.
The same code positive in one document and negative in another, or the same procedure with two dates. Confirm in the text only: differences from the JSON are false alarms for the metric.
Run all diagnoses, procedures, drugs and measurements through the slot menu. Anything that maps to no slot is a missing slot type; add general slots, not patient-specific ones.
The README says fragments such as 'zur sonographisch' appear as procedures. Drop concepts with no code and no recognisable term before using the JSON as a hint.
It can contain markup such as spellcorrection spans and extra spaces. Compute spans and quotes on one canonical text (entities decoded, tags stripped, whitespace collapsed).

label_display_rules.detail: Official product information (SmPC, section 4.3 Contraindications; section 4.4 warnings). In production use the Austrian Fachinformation from the BASG register (L10). The prototype uses EU or UK labels for the same ingredient (L01-L09).
Match the shown medication to a label through the generic name or ATC code, never the brand string. Brand names in the notes are only search aids.

Contraindications (section 4.3) are shown as 'listed contraindications'. Warnings (section 4.4 or 4.2) are shown separately and only in long mode or when the task matches (for example contrast imaging).
Each listed item is shown with the related patient facts: found (with source link), documented as none, or not documented. The screen never says a drug is contraindicated for this patient.
P1 items only, and only where the related slot is found or not documented. The panel is collapsed with a count badge.
All items, warnings, and population items (pregnancy, children). Population items are hidden when the age rule excludes them.

Interaction contraindications (for example candesartan with aliskiren in diabetes, aspirin with methotrexate at 15 mg per week or more) run as code over the medication list and diabetes or kidney facts.
Every panel names the label used, its authority and date, and links to it. Era note: label text is current, while the 2015-2016 prescriber used the label of that time.
Different products of one ingredient can list different contraindications (for example some aspirin labels also list concurrent oral anticoagulation). Never merge labels silently.
BNF and BNFC content (L12). Commercial drug databases unless licensed.

drug_contraindications.era_note: Current label text. Some older or generic labels list iodinated contrast in section 4.3; the current Glucophage text puts it in section 4.4 as stop-around-imaging advice.

listed_contraindications.text: Hypersensitivity to metformin or an excipient
Any acute metabolic acidosis, such as lactic acidosis or ketoacidosis
Diabetic pre-coma
Severe renal failure (GFR below 30 mL/min)
Acute conditions that can alter kidney function: dehydration, severe infection, shock
Disease that can cause tissue hypoxia: decompensated heart failure, respiratory failure, recent myocardial infarction, shock
Hepatic insufficiency, acute alcohol intoxication, alcoholism

label_warnings.text: Iodinated contrast: the label advises stopping metformin at or before the imaging procedure and not restarting for at least 48 hours, once kidney function is re-checked and stable (section 4.4).

Surgery under general, spinal or epidural anaesthesia: the label advises stopping at the time of surgery and restarting no earlier than 48 hours after surgery or resuming oral food, once kidney function is confirmed.
